description: Language-neutral golden vectors for the Social Security engine. Canonical copy lives in the Social Security Optimizer repo; the Finance Tracker copies this file and runs the engine-rule cases against backend/ss_optimizer.py. Expected values are hand-derived from the cited statute/POMS/IRS source, not from engine output.

conventions.household: Annual simulation. Inputs are snake_case. persons.{a,b} = {birth_year, pia, life_expectancy}. 'monthly_X_at_age' maps person X's age in a calendar year to the monthly benefit paid that year (benefit_X / 12). 'monthly_X_in_year' maps a calendar year to the monthly benefit. cola=0 so dollar basis does not affect results. A person is alive in every year where age <= life_expectancy.
conventions.rounding: PIA truncated to the dime; monthly benefits floored to the dollar.

cases.source: SSA Act 202(q), 202(w); 20 CFR 404.410, 404.313; FRA 67 for births 1960+ (SSA Act 216(l))
FRA 66 and 8 months for 1958 births (SSA Act 216(l)); 56 months early = 36 x 5/9% + 20 x 5/12%; 4 and 40 months of DRC at 2/3% per month
FRA 66 for 1943-1954 births; 48 months early = 25%; 48 months DRC = 32%
SSA Act 215(a)(1); bend points for eligibility year 2026 = $1,286 / $7,749 (ssa.gov/oact/COLA/bendpoints.html). 0.9x1286 + 0.32x6463 + 0.15x251 = 3263.21 -> 3263.20
Bend points for eligibility year 2027 = $1,340 / $8,077. 0.9x1340 + 0.32x6660 = 3337.20
Eligibility after the latest published bend point year: latest bend points with indexing frozen at latest AWI (SSA statement convention)

SSA Act 215(b); 20 CFR 404.211. Born 1960: indexing year 2020, bend points 2022 ($1,024 / $6,172). 1950 is before the 1951 computation period and is excluded. 1980: min(30000, cap 25900) x AWI2020 55628.60 / AWI1980 12513.46 = 115138.48. 2021: after the indexing year, nominal 100000. AIME = floor(215138.48 / 420) = 512; PIA at eligibility (2022) = 0.9 x 512 = 460.80; with the COLAs of Dec 2022-2025 (8.7, 3.2, 2.5, 2.8%, each truncated to the dime) = 500.80, 516.80, 529.70, 544.50 in 2026 dollars (SSA Act 215(i)).

SSA Act 215(i); COLAs effective December of each year from the eligibility year (2020) through 2025 (1.3, 5.9, 8.7, 3.2, 2.5, 2.8%; ssa.gov/oact/cola/colaseries.html), each step truncated to the dime: 3039.0, 3218.3, 3498.2, 3610.1, 3700.3, 3803.9
Eligibility (2035) after the basis year: no COLAs apply yet

Spousal excess payable only once the worker has filed (deemed filing, BBA 2015 sec. 831; 20 CFR 404.623); reduction based on months of spousal entitlement before FRA (SSA Act 202(q); 20 CFR 404.410). B files at 62 (own 70% of 1000 = 700); A files at 70 when B is 70, so the 1000 excess is unreduced.

Widow(er) benefit = 100% of deceased PIA, reduced for survivor age (28.5% at 60, prorated to survivor FRA; SSA Act 202(e)(2), 202(q)); limited by RIB-LIM to the larger of the deceased's reduced benefit or 82.5% of PIA (SSA Act 202(e)(2)(D); POMS RS 00615.320). While both are alive (age 63), B gets own 700 plus the spousal excess (2000 - 1000) reduced 35% for starting at 62 = 650, total 1350. A dies after age 63; B starts survivor benefits at 64: 4000 x (1 - 0.285 x 36/84) = 3511.43, limited to max(2800, 3300) = 3300.

Survivor at/after survivor FRA receives the deceased's benefit including delayed retirement credits (SSA Act 202(e)(2)(C), 202(w)). Before the death, B's spousal excess (1500 - 1000) starts at 70 when A files, unreduced.

If the worker dies before FRA without having claimed, the widow(er) base is 100% of PIA (no DRCs, no RIB-LIM). The survivor start age is chosen by value (0% return, B alive through 90): start 65 = 2755 x 26 = 71,630; 66 = 2877 x 25 = 71,925; 67 = 3000 x 24 = 72,000 -> wait for the unreduced benefit at survivor FRA 67.

A (1965) claims at FRA 67 in 2032 and is alive through age 68 (2033). B (1970, survivor FRA 67) claimed own at 62: 800 x 0.70 = 560; spousal excess 700 from 62, 60 months early = 35% reduction -> 455. A dead from 2034 (B age 64). Survivor start age is chosen by value (0% return, B alive through 70): start 64 = 3000 x (1 - 0.285 x 36/84) = 2633 x 7 yrs = 18,431; 65 = 2755 x 6 + 560 = 17,090; 66 = 2877 x 5 + 1,120 = 15,505; 67 = 3000 x 4 + 1,680 = 13,680 -> start at 64. A claimed at FRA so no RIB-LIM. Survivor may start at 60+ independently of own benefit (SSA Act 202(e); POMS RS 00615.301).

Same household with B alive through 90 (0% return): start 64 = 2633 x 27 = 71,091; 65 = 2755 x 26 + 560 = 72,190; 66 = 2877 x 25 + 1,120 = 73,045; 67 = 3000 x 24 + 1,680 = 73,680 -> wait for the unreduced survivor benefit at survivor FRA 67, keeping own 560 until then.
Model assumption: payable-benefit factor applied only from the solvency start year onward (2026 Trustees Report projects OASI reserve depletion in 2032).
IRC 86(b)(2)(B): tax-exempt interest counts in provisional income. PI = 20000 + 10000 + 15000 = 45000; 0.85 x 11000 + 4500 = 13850 < 25500
